foundation_models.article_summary: The article argues Gemma 4 was fine for one-shot prompts but failed badly in agentic coding workflows, especially tool-call loops and repeated command generation.
foundation_models.newsworthy_attributes: Reported to get stuck in infinite loops, leak prompt text into output, and fail tool calls; contrasted unfavorably with Qwen 3.6 on agent benchmarks and MCPMark.
foundation_models.supporting_snippet: “Gemma 4 was the worst version of this pattern... it would start confidently, then lose track of what it was doing... tool call failures and command repetition that made the model unusable for agent work.”

foundation_models.article_summary: The article presents Qwen 3.6-35B-A3B as the first open-source model the author found that actually works for agentic coding workflows, especially local tool-using tasks.
foundation_models.newsworthy_attributes: Sparse MoE model with 35B total / 3B active parameters; benchmarked above Gemma 4 on MCPMark, SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and NL2Repo; downloadable and usable locally.
foundation_models.supporting_snippet: “Qwen 3.6–35B-A3B has 35 billion total parameters, but only 3 billion of them are active... On SWE-bench Verified... Qwen scores 73.4. Gemma scores 52.0... I downloaded Qwen 3.6–35B-A3B... It read the CSV... No loops. No gibberish.”

glossary.proposed_definition: An architecture where only a subset of experts/parameters are active per token, enabling smaller active compute than the total parameter count.
glossary.supporting_snippet: “Qwen 3.6–35B-A3B has 35 billion total parameters, but only 3 billion of them are active for any given token you send it... The architecture is called Mixture of Experts.”
